title: Erasing one bit must release a minimum of heat
body: Landauer's principle (1961) sets the floor: erasing a bit at temperature T costs at least kT ln 2 of energy as heat, because compressing information states raises entropy elsewhere. Computation that never erases can, in principle, sidestep it. It ties information to thermodynamics with an equation, not a metaphor, and experiments have since brushed against the bound.
